title.label: Great; gripes are in the minutiae

content.label:
Ok this app is getting 5 stars because it is simple and straightforward. Well featured and robust details without too much clutter. I like it a lot and have been using it very well.

My minor gripe is that the apple watch app has slightly different controls, and I develop conflicting user habits since I use both mobile and watch apps every day. For example the watch app scrolls up and down to change pages (which I actually like better!) while the mobile app changes pages by horizontal flipping of cards. Same with click to complete vs. press and hold to complete.
Very minor details but since I’m doing them so often, it is burdensome to get confused trying to quickly complete tasks. For example, accidentally clicking instead of press and holding on a task to complete it in the mobile app will cycle the task view to the calendar and subsequent options. One misclick can have you cycle through 3-4 alternate task views before you can return to the normal one and complete the task, turning a 2-second interaction into a 5-second one. Again, it adds up, which is why I am here writing this.

I would prefer to just do a better job automating completions to avoid having to click to complete tasks in the first place, but the shortcuts app has limited options.

title.label: A Good App that Keeps Getting Better

content.label:
I used to use this app a lot back in 2009 when it was a free app, and in its infancy. When the phone I was using back then died, I forgot to reinstall it. 

I went on about my life, relying on my calendar and memo and list-making apps, and setting a million different alarms on my phone. 

While those systems have all worked well for me, I found myself, recently, wanting to know at a glance how often I was doing certain things, and I remembered how much I had liked using this app. 

I looked it up, saw that the developers had made some changes that appealed to me, and that it is now a paid app. 

I feel it is not too expensive for something that solidly and consistently helps *me* to be more solid and consistent in the ways I show up in my life. I’m glad to see the ways that it has become a stronger app since the last time I used it regularly. I like it a lot.

You can choose to mark a day as incomplete, the app works on  MacOS, WatchOS, and iOS which is so helpful for me. I love the different display options on the watch which helps me to see what I need for tasks I want to do. You can choose so many options for how you want to do your streaks for example you can choose to do specific amount of days in a fortnight which is perfect for me since there is only a certain amount of days every two weeks that I have my children and want to do things with them.  The stats are great and I find the colors and four pages so helpful to put things in different categories. The syncing between devices is wonderful and the support has been fast and helpful to find hidden features like marking a task as skipped on the day it happens rather than going back and doing that. The developer has put a lot of love, time, and energy into this app. 

I have no association with the developer but I will add that the other apps are also very good.
